clue.text: Harry has been one of the Wailers

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and trouble, so the letters that follow are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone called Harry once played in Bob Marley's band, the Wailers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a man's name, but it is a verb here. The Wailers are not the reggae band but anything that wails.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore this female spirit wails to foretell a death, so she is literally a wailer.

clue.text: Brutal acts affected arbiter with bias

indicators.note: something affected has been altered or put on, so the letters are changed in arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A referee whose bias shows commits cruel deeds in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' reads as describing the referee's acts, but it is the signal to rearrange the two following words together.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun for savage, cruel deeds; barbarity is the quality of uncivilised cruelty.

clue.text: Some number on street work without breaks

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in algebra
taken as written
standard abbreviation for street
OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Several people on a particular street keep working without a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some number' is N, the mathematician's indefinite number, not NO; 'on' is then taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective meaning continuing with no pauses or interruptions, as in a direct flight or ceaseless chatter.

clue.text: Structured affair and ruptured her chair rhyme essentially

indicators.note: something ruptured is burst apart, so its letters can be reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written, eight letters to rearrange

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the very centre letter is wanted

parts.note: the central letter of the five-letter word

explanation.surface: A poem about a broken chair turns into an oddly organised business.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opening two words; 'and' joins it to the wordplay, which is an eight-letter rearrangement plus a single centre letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A system ranking people or things in graded levels is an organised arrangement, so a structured affair in loose terms.

clue.text: Titillate former lover on call

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to cite is to call or summon someone, as to court

explanation.surface: An old flame stirs up feelings with a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to arouse or stimulate someone's interest or feelings, often with a sexual flavour.

clue.text: Top Catholic shot earl

parts.note: a pop is a shot, as from a gun
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A senior Catholic gunned down a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a past-tense verb about the earl, but it is a noun giving the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of the Roman Catholic Church sits at the summit of its clergy.

clue.text: Penny greeting Greek character

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny
a common word of greeting

explanation.surface: A woman named Penny says hello to someone from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name, but it is the coin, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the twenty-first letter of the Greek alphabet, and a character can mean a written letter.

clue.text: Nudges exhausted executives to support parking fine

parts.note: P is the map symbol for parking
OK means fine or all right

indicators.note: exhausted means emptied out, so the inside of the word is removed and only its outer pair stays

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Tired bosses are prodded into backing a parking ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'to support' puts the outer letters underneath the other two pieces. 'Fine' looks like a penalty next to 'parking', but it means all right.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for prodding someone lightly with a finger or elbow, third person singular.

clue.text: Aga perhaps fled Greek empire originally

parts.note: ran away means fled
G is the abbreviation for Greek

indicators.note: originally points to how a word begins, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An Ottoman aga ran away from the Greek empire at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: An aga was an Ottoman commander, which suits the Greek empire, but here an Aga is a heavy British cast-iron kitchen cooker brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large cooking stove with ovens and hotplates, and the Aga is the best-known example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Game animal that hops and jumps

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a chirping insect related to the grasshopper

explanation.walkthrough: 'Game animal' reads as something hunted, but the split falls after the first word: a sport, then a leaping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names an English bat-and-ball sport played with wickets and a small leaping, chirping insect.

clue.text: Kitchen appliance overwhelms staff chap hosting dinner

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf completely, so one piece swallows another whole

parts.note: a machine for browning bread
a mast is a tall pole, a staff for a flag

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget overpowers the workers of a man throwing a dinner party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees but it is a pole; the appliance splits after its fifth letter to take it in.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the person who presides at a formal dinner, introducing speakers and proposing toasts.

clue.text: Colonist seen in Barnet periodically

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A settler spotted now and then in Barnet, a district of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London borough; the even letters of the name give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect lives in large organised colonies, so crossword setters cheekily call it a colonist.

clue.text: Plant I encountered by river over in Asia

indicators.note: put in something means placed inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the letters run the opposite way

parts.note: taken as written
met means encountered
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A traveller describes coming across a plant beside a river in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The first three short pieces join, flip, and go inside the continent after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia is a genus of aromatic herbs and shrubs including wormwood, mugwort and tarragon.

clue.text: Teach sumo wrestling for Fu Manchu?

indicators.note: wrestlers twist and tangle together, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is giving sumo lessons to the fictional villain Fu Manchu.
explanation.walkthrough: Fu Manchu here is not the villain but the long drooping style of facial hair named after him; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Fu Manchu is a style of thin, long, downward-hanging whiskers on the upper lip, so it exemplifies the answer.

clue.text: Setter's stated full consequences

definitions.note: the plural definition matches the answer used as a collective noun for effects

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I, so the setter is means I am, contracted

indicators.note: something stated is spoken out, so the answer is spelt like a phrase said out loud

parts.note: packed means full

explanation.surface: The puzzle maker says the results were complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter's' is the contraction for 'the setter is', that is 'I'm', not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The impact of a decision is its effect or the results that follow from it.

clue.text: Some in Paris got to accept United manager's position?

parts.note: du is French for 'some', as in du pain

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for United in football club names

explanation.surface: Some people in Paris had to welcome the Manchester United boss's job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manchester United manager's position' sounds like a job title; the question mark signals the place the manager physically sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A football manager sits in the sheltered, sunken bench area beside the pitch during matches.

clue.text: Best choose one, mother!

parts.note: to opt is to choose
Roman numeral for one
mum is British for mother

explanation.surface: A child urges Mum to pick the finest one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adverb on 'choose', but it stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means most favourable or ideal, the very finest possible.

clue.text: Celebrity was up gathering information

indicators.note: gathering means collecting in, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: a team that was up on points led
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A famous person stayed awake collecting news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was up' suggests being awake, but it means being ahead in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a very famous person, someone renowned in their field.

clue.text: Yearning to get away? Small cost when cycling

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the leading letter goes round to the back

parts.note: titchy is British slang for tiny
a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: A traveller longs for a holiday but notes that bike touring is cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: The joined pieces have their first letter moved to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes restlessness and a strong urge to travel or move on somewhere new.

clue.text: Caught when tricks get played somewhere near Naples

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
April 1st, April Fools' Day, written as APR I

explanation.surface: Someone is caught out by pranks in a spot near Naples.
explanation.walkthrough: April Fools' Day is when pranks are played; it is written as the month abbreviation plus Roman numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: This rocky island lies in the Bay of Naples, just off the Sorrento peninsula in southern Italy.

clue.text: Starts to treat everyone attending meal

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so each word gives its first

parts.note: first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A host begins treating all the guests at a dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain tea can be an evening or afternoon meal, not just the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a light afternoon meal, or in northern Britain the main evening meal.

clue.text: Final drink, on me?

parts.note: to sup is to drink
re means on or about
taken as written

explanation.surface: A barman calls last orders and offers the last round himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink on me' sounds like buying a round; 'on' is RE, meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means highest or ultimate, as in a supreme court whose verdict is the last word.

clue.text: Bit of breakfast for one grand?

parts.note: e.g. means for example, 'for one'
G is short for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A breakfast that costs a thousand pounds per person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For one' suggests a single serving, but it is the abbreviation for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled or fried hen's product is a typical component of a cooked morning meal.

clue.text: Heavenly body this writer gets into bed

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
the writer refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: The writer slips into bed beside a gorgeous partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly body' is a flirtatious phrase for an attractive person, but here it means an astronomical object.
explanation.definitionFit: An icy object orbiting the Sun with a glowing tail is an astronomical body in the sky.

clue.text: Part of chicken claw in gourmet sandwiches?

indicators.note: to sandwich is to enclose between two layers, so the answer is held within the text

parts.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: A fancy deli puts chicken claws in its sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like food in the scene, but it is a verb meaning encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: The limb a bird flies with is a common cut of chicken meat.

clue.text: Scarlet's back to collect 500 sheets one imagines

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so one piece is enclosed by the other
going back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
a ream is 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Scarlett O'Hara is back to pick up a big pile of paper, or so one supposes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scarlet's' is 'Scarlet is'; a ream is the standard stationery bundle of 500 sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition reads 'one who imagines': a person given to fantasies and visions.
